title: From Spoon to Silverware: Patterson's Stadium Landslide
title_candidates: From Spoon to Silverware: Patterson's Stadium Landslide
Eleven at the Thirteenth: How Catalunya Changed Hands
A 12, an 11 and a Course Record: TEG 12 in Full
Patterson 172, and the Sound of Williams's Eleven
theme: Catalunya punished everybody — the difference was who kept getting back up. John Patterson made a 12 and two 10s and still never posted a below-median round; Gregg Williams was immaculate for two days and then lost twelve shots in three holes on the Stadium. The Trophy went to the man least damaged by his own disasters — the same man who finished stone last at TEG 10.
opening_hook: Open on the Tour course scoreboard nobody was reading — Patterson signing for a 45 with a 12 on it — and promise the Stadium's 13th, where the tournament actually turned; then run the four rounds in order so the R3 detonation lands in sequence.
foreshadow: R1 H4 on the Tour: Patterson takes 12 at a par 4 (SI 2), the worst hole of the entire TEG — and it barely dents him
Williams goes 14 holes in R1 without dropping a net shot and signs a personal-best +12 gross; nobody looked less likely to give anything back
Stuart Neumann's R1: a 12 at the 15th, a 10 at the 13th and a 105 — a new course-worst at the Tour across 10 prior visits
David Mullin, reigning Wooden Spoon holder and winner of eight Green Jackets, arrives at Camiral quietly leading the gross early on R1

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.how: Level-ish for two rounds on the Tour — Williams led by exactly one point after both R1 and R2, with 18 lead changes of no real consequence. On the Stadium in R3 Patterson posted 45, best in the field, nine clear of Williams, taking the outright lead at H4 as Williams's round disintegrated (9 at the 4th, then 12 shots gone across 11-13 including an 11). A 1-point deficit became an 8-point lead in an afternoon. Patterson then posted the best round in the field again in R4 (40) to stretch it to 10. Built, not inherited: two best-in-field rounds, no below-median rounds, a round-to-round spread of 5 against a field median of 8.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.how: Baker led the gross from R1 H16, lost it to Williams at R3 H3 after 23 holes in front (b25), and took it straight back at R3 H4 — never to be threatened again. Three best-in-field gross rounds out of four, a spread of 6 against a field median of 10, and a finish for the ages: 89 at the Stadium in R4, a new course record beating the 90 that had stood across 15 prior visits. Mullin, the eight-time Jacket holder, was runner-up by 8 and could not have flipped it even by replacing his worst round with his own average.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Alex Baker was bottom after each of the first three rounds; Mullin took the position for the first time all tournament at R4 H3 and never got off it. The mechanism is in the anatomy: Mullin was below the field median in all four rounds, with a spread of 10 (field median 8), and inherited last place rather than being caught — Alex Baker outscored him in two of four rounds and still finished behind. The decisive stretch is R4 holes 3-5: a 9, an 8 and a double, ten shots gone in three holes. His birdie-laced 14 points across 11-14 later the same afternoon arrived precisely too late. Back-to-back Spoons for the reigning holder.

rounds.angle: Baker breaks the Stadium record with 89 while Mullin breaks himself at 3-5 and inherits the Spoon; Patterson posts another field-best round to win by 10, and Neumann's eagle at the 15th supplies the day's only genuine joy.

players.arc: Last of six at TEG 10, fourth at TEG 11, and now Trophy champion by ten — a 12, two 10s and not a single below-median round, which is the whole story of TEG 12 in one card.

Three-time Trophy winner who played the best golf of his life for two days on the Tour (PB +12 round, PB +76 total, two new course bests) and then lost the tournament in three holes at the Stadium's 11th, 12th and 13th.

The defending Trophy champion could not repeat, but he was the best ball-striker in Catalonia from first hole to last — three best-in-field gross rounds and an 89 that is now the Stadium course record.
Eight Green Jackets, a course PB at the Tour, second in the gross — and a second consecutive Wooden Spoon, sealed by ten shots lost between the 3rd and 5th on the final afternoon.
Opened with a 105 that is a new Tour course-worst and closed with an eagle at the Stadium's 15th and a personal course best of 96: the widest emotional range in the field, and still no silverware.

Bottom of the pile after each of the first three rounds and somehow not the Spoon holder — rescued by his brother's course, a final-round 93 and a 13-shot improvement on his last visit to the Stadium.

venue_notes: TEG's 3rd visit to Catalonia. R1-R2 on the Tour course (the 3rd and 4th TEG rounds there), R2 described as the 'more forgiving' sibling — worth noting it produced Patterson's 12, Neumann's 12 and 10, and a new course-worst 105. R3-R4 on the Stadium (the 4th and 5th TEG rounds there), Spain's premier course, where the Trophy, the Jacket and the Spoon were all actually settled — and where Jon Baker took the course record down to 89.
course_history_notes: Jon Baker's 89 in R4 is a new PGA Catalunya - Stadium course record across 15 prior visits, beating 90 — and his own new personal best there.
Stuart Neumann's 105 in R1 is a new Tour course-worst across 10 prior visits, exceeding the previous 103; he then set a personal Stadium best of 96 in R4.
Gregg Williams set personal course bests on both layouts — 84 at the Tour in R1 (8 better than TEG 6) and 92 at the Stadium in R4 (7 better than TEG 11).
John Patterson improved his Tour best by 7 (96) and his Stadium best by 4 (95); Alex Baker was 13 shots better than his last Stadium visit with a 93.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R3 H4 at the Stadium — Patterson takes the outright lead as Williams signs for a quintuple-bogey 9, and by the 13th (Williams's 11) the one-point gap has become eight.
Green Jacket: R3 H4 — Jon Baker takes back the gross lead he had surrendered at R3 H3 after 23 holes in front, and is never headed again over the remaining 33 holes.
Wooden Spoon: R4 H3 — Mullin's quadruple-bogey 9 at the 3rd starts a run of ten shots lost in three holes and drops him to last for the first time all tournament; he stays there.

payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided / Trophy section
payoffs.payoff: The worst hole of the TEG belonged to the champion — and he still shot 45. It becomes the proof of the theme: no below-median rounds, a spread of 5, disaster absorbed rather than compounded.

payoffs.seed: Williams's 14 clean holes and PB +12 in R1
payoffs.payoff: The most reliable man in Catalonia loses twelve shots across 11-13, including an 11 at the par-4 13th, and hands over a lead he had held since R1.

payoffs.seed: Neumann's 105 and the two double-figure holes in R1
payoffs.payoff: The same player eagles the par-5 15th at the Stadium — the field's only eagle of the TEG — and posts a personal course best of 96.

payoffs.seed: Mullin, reigning Spoon holder, leading the gross early in R1
payoffs.payoff: He finishes second in the Jacket by 8 and collects a second consecutive Wooden Spoon, sunk by holes 3-5 on the final afternoon and by four straight below-median rounds.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Inversion is really only 'defending champ didn't repeat' — Jon Baker still won the Jacket with a course record, so nothing was inverted; the better frame is Patterson, last of six at TEG 10, winning by ten (underdog) with Williams's R3 as the tragic pivot.

why_the_champion_won: Patterson built it rather than inherited it: two best-in-field rounds, not one round below the field median, and a round-to-round spread of 5 against a field median of 8 — so when Williams lost twelve shots in three holes on the Stadium, Patterson was the one standing there to take nine points out of him in a single round, and Williams could not have flipped it even by replacing his worst round with his own average.
